title: Organization detail — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of organization-detail-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema — no implementation, no package.json, no node_modules — so every constraint here is READ BY A PERSON AND HAND-IMPLEMENTED. A `required` list is an instruction someone will follow literally, with no validator to disagree with the prose (.claude/rules/workflow.md §12).

organizationId.description: Opaque, non-sequential, unguessable. Never parsed, decoded or interpreted by a client.

membershipRole.$comment: `extensible`, and the argument is an OPEN QUESTION rather than a plan: `permission-catalog.yaml` AZ11 records that `authorization/roles.ts` is a closed TypeScript union of two while `0007` D10 says 'roles are data, never code — customers modify or replace them freely', and that `0023`'s trigger to reconcile them has already fired. A third membership role is the expected outcome of that reconciliation, not a hypothetical. A client that broke when one appeared would make a data change into a client release.
membershipRole.description: The closed union stored on organization_membership.role (docs/decisions/0019). AN UNRECOGNISED STORED VALUE IS NEVER RENDERED: it collapses to null internally and denies everything, so a row written by a future migration this build does not understand cannot reach a client as an unknown string.

organizationDetailOutput.description: EVERYTHING THE DETAIL PAGE NEEDS, IN ONE RESPONSE — the Template is embedded rather than returned as an id to fetch, because a read costs writes in this class and a three-request page spends three times the budget. NOTE WHAT IS STRUCTURALLY ABSENT AND CANNOT BE ADDED: no workspaces, no customers, no counts of either, no activity, no usage, no last-seen. Those live behind `whereWithTenant` and a platform route holds no tenant handle, so they are unreachable rather than withheld. AND NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT BY RULING: no member list. See theMembershipRuling — an operator can enumerate every Organization, so member lists over all of them invert to every principal's Organization list, which core-object-registry.yaml CO1 forbids by name.

status.$comment: DUPLICATED with `platform-operator-v1`'s `organizationStatus` — same two values, same wire field, and both must carry this policy. `extensible` because suspension already has a named future route and the permission catalogue states that `core.platform-organization.update` DOES NOT COVER STATUS, so a third state arrives by a separate decision rather than never. Do not read Core's refusal to render an unrecognised STORED value as making this closed: that is schema-drift protection and answers a different question from whether a new value may be added.

display_name.description:
THE ORGANIZATION'S NAME. AMENDED 2026-09-07 by organization-identity-v1 and docs/decisions/0031; the canonical definition is urn:dudo:schema:organization-identity:1#/$defs/displayName, restated here rather than $ref'd because no URN resolver exists (AS1), and the 200 bound is the one this field already published.

THIS PREVIOUSLY READ 'ALWAYS null today — control-plane/0002_organization.sql declined a name column and THE ORGANIZATION-STRUCTURE SLICE OWNS IT.' THE SECOND HALF IS THE PART THAT HAD TO GO: it pointed a reader at a slice that had not happened, and the contract that owns this field now exists. THE FIRST HALF IS STILL TRUE UNTIL THE COLUMN LANDS — null on every response until control-plane/0002_organization.sql gains the column and an operator sets a value.

NULL MEANS NO NAME HAS BEEN RECORDED. REQUIRED AND NULLABLE rather than optional, so that names arriving change no shape and no client has to learn a new field.

*** THE NAMELESS SET IS OPEN TODAY. *** `organization-onboarding-v1` accepts `display_name` and does not require it, on the Team Lead's sequencing ruling of 2026-09-07, so EVERY NEW ORGANIZATION CAN BE NAMELESS until `ON-7` is discharged. It closes at three when onboarding tightens.

CORRECTED 2026-09-07, SECOND HOME OF THE SAME CLAIM. This read *"reachable only for Organizations created before onboarding required one, so the nameless set is CLOSED and shrinks"* — the identical false statement of fact `qa-agent` found in `organization-identity-v1`, written into two schemas on one day by one author. `workflow.md` §12: budget for more homes than you find. A client MUST NOT assume a name is present on a recently created Organization.

A client renders organization_id verbatim when this is null and MUST NOT substitute a placeholder of its own, or two consoles will invent two different ones. That obligation is unchanged.

commercial_registration.description:
The Bahrain Commercial Registration (CR), issued through Sijilat. ADDED 2026-09-07 by organization-identity-v1. Operator-entered and recorded; there is no Sijilat API and no integration is proposed. A THREE-STATE UNION — `not_recorded`, `not_registered`, `registered` — because 'we never asked' and 'they told us they have none' are different facts. Every Organization is `not_recorded` until an operator sets it.

IT IS A CONTROL-PLANE COLUMN, which is why it passes organization-detail-v1's own test — a field is available to an operator if and only if reading it requires no tenant store. NOT because a registration number is 'less sensitive' than a Workspace name: theWorkspaceFinding is explicit that the structure-versus-content intuition is what the tenancy model ignores.

vat_registration.description:
The VAT account number issued by the National Bureau for Revenue. ADDED 2026-09-07 by organization-identity-v1. Operator-entered. `not_registered` IS A LEGITIMATE PERMANENT STATE rather than an unfilled field — Bahrain VAT registration is mandatory above an annual-supplies threshold and voluntary below it — so a client that treats it as missing data will keep prompting a customer who has already answered.

THERE IS NO DIGIT COUNT IN THE FORMAT AND THE ABSENCE IS A RULING. See organization-identity-v1's theFormatRuling: a pattern is a refusal, and an at-count pattern that is wrong refuses a LEGAL registration.

template.description: The Template this Organization adopted, RESOLVED AND EMBEDDED. Null when none was recorded — every Organization created before Templates existed, which today is all of them. Embedding is safe because a Template is tenant-INDEPENDENT platform configuration, identical for every caller, so it copies nothing sensitive and creates no staleness a client could act on wrongly.

level_labels.description: Fully populated, with platform defaults filled in for any level the Template omitted — the client never implements the default table, which is what stops the web and Apple consoles drifting into two ideas of what an unlabelled level is called.

member_count.description: HOW MANY PRINCIPALS BELONG TO THIS ORGANIZATION. A COUNT, NEVER A LIST, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE RULING: a count does not invert, so it reconstructs nothing about any principal, while a list over every Organization reconstructs every principal's Organization list. It answers what an operator legitimately asks — did onboarding work, is this Organization in use, is it abandoned — without naming anyone. ITS SMALL LEAK IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: repeated reads reveal that membership changed, never who or in which direction, which is a fact about the Organization rather than about a person.

resolveMemberInput.$comment:
PHASE 3 OF docs/decisions/0034 LANDED 2026-09-09: THE DEPRECATED `identifier` ALIAS IS REMOVED. This is the BREAKING phase; phases 1 and 2 were additive and are what made it safe.

*** IT IS REMOVED, NOT TOMBSTONED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. *** There is no `_removed_identifier` in `properties`. Under `additionalProperties: false` a tombstone is A PERMITTED OPTIONAL FIELD — `workflow.md` §12: the same defect one size smaller. The removal is recorded HERE, in a `$comment`, which is not a constraint and cannot be sent.

WHAT WENT, EXACTLY: the property `identifier`, and the `oneOf` over two single-element `required` branches that expressed the both-present refusal. The outer object now carries `required: ["target_identifier"]` — with one name there is nothing to be exactly-one BETWEEN, so the `oneOf` has no work left and keeping it would be a two-branch construction over a one-member set.

THE EXPRESSED/EXECUTED DISTINCTION THAT LIVED HERE IS NOT LOST, BECAUSE IT WAS NEVER ABOUT THIS FIELD. It said: STATED in prose, EXPRESSED as `oneOf`, EXECUTED by Core and by nothing else — no validator in this repository runs JSON Schema (`packages/contracts/README.md`), so an implementer still has to write every refusal. THAT REMAINS TRUE OF `required` ITSELF: a missing `target_identifier` is refused because CORE REFUSES IT, not because this line executes. The axes are independent (`workflow.md` §12), and the danger was specific — a reader who trusts the machine-readable form concludes the rule is handled and never checks that Core implemented it.

SATISFIABILITY IS UNAFFECTED AND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `target_identifier` is present in `properties`, so a `required` naming it is satisfiable under `packages/testing/suites/contracts/satisfiability.ts` — a check that DOES execute. The previous empty outer `required` existed because the requirement lived in the branches; with the branches gone it moves back out.
resolveMemberInput.description:
*** THE RENAME IS COMPLETE. `target_identifier` IS THE ONLY NAME THIS ROUTE ACCEPTS. *** Phase 3 of docs/decisions/0034 landed 2026-09-09, removing the deprecated `identifier` alias from this contract and from Core's route table IN ONE CHANGE — `check-route-fields.mjs` compares the two and goes red if they are split, which is the check working rather than an obstacle.

WHAT THE THREE PHASES WERE, KEPT BECAUSE THE SEQUENCE IS THE REUSABLE PART: Core accepted both names → the console switched → both sides dropped the old one. **A change that is correct in isolation is an outage when one side is already deployed**, and the order is always widen, switch, narrow. This contract set sequenced around that shape three times in one day.

*** A STRAGGLER STILL SENDING `identifier` NOW RECEIVES `invalid_argument`, BEFORE AUTHENTICATION, AND THAT IS THE PRICED RESIDUAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. *** It is loud, recoverable and immediately diagnosable. `OD-5`'s original precondition — Core recording which spelling arrived — was WITHDRAWN on 2026-09-08 and must not be built: the sender population is closed by AUTHENTICATION rather than by policy, so it is enumerable rather than measurable. Reaching this route needs a `platform_operator` row, and `0024`'s mutual exclusion means such a principal holds no `organization_membership`, so no tenant client can authenticate here at all. That leaves one console, the scripts, and one or two named operators.

*** THIS IS NOT THE COLLISION `architecture.md` §1a FORBIDS, AND THE DISTINCTION IS EXACT. *** §1a's defect was ONE NAME MEANING TWO DIFFERENT PARTIES — `identifier` as the caller's own in `confirmation-v1` and as the target's here, which made the merged route return `forbidden` on every well-formed request. THIS IS TWO NAMES MEANING THE SAME PARTY: a deprecation alias, not a shared namespace with two owners. Stated because the next reader will otherwise apply §1a to it and conclude we broke our own rule. The reservation §1a creates is unaffected — `identifier` remains forbidden as a NEW field name anywhere, and this is an old one being retired.

RENAMED FROM `identifier` ON 2026-09-05 UNDER THE PLATFORM-WIDE RESERVATION. It means THE TARGET'S — the principal being resolved — and a field naming a principal must say which principal. This route is not gated today, so there was no live defect; it was one gating decision away from being the same semantic collision that made credential-reset-v1 unbuildable, because confirmation-v1 would then have stripped it as the caller's own. The rule is deliberately not scoped to 'contracts that compose with a cross-cutting mechanism': that scope depends on `sensitivity: critical`, which a route ACQUIRES LATER, so such a rule would be correct the day it was written and silently wrong the first time a route became critical.

THE OPERATOR MUST ALREADY KNOW THE IDENTIFIER — the customer gave it to them. That requirement IS the control this route rests on: an operator resolving an identifier they were given is support; an operator receiving a list they did not ask for by name is surveillance. The Organization is a path parameter, not a body field.

target_identifier.description:
A login identifier. THE CANONICAL DEFINITION IS urn:dudo:schema:account-identifier:1#/$defs/accountIdentifier; this is a restatement of it, character-identical by obligation, restated rather than $ref'd because no URN resolver exists (AS1).

CORRECTED 2026-09-05: the pattern was ^[!-?A-~]*@[!-?A-~]*$, which encodes EXACTLY ONE '@' — stricter than credential-store.ts, which requires at least one and never counts. RFC 5321 permits a quoted local part containing '@', so the old pattern refused legal addresses that Core accepts. ADDITIVE, since it widens.

THE ENFORCEMENT GAP THIS ROUTE SITS ON, STATED BECAUSE IT INTERACTS WITH THE FIVE-WAY COLLAPSE: platform/core/directory/member-resolution.ts:157 calls normalizeIdentifier WITHOUT calling isSubmittableIdentifier first, so Core does not today enforce this shape on this route — the only live check is client-side. While that holds, a principal the console cannot type is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, which is a SECOND collapse layered on the designed one. The remedy is Core enforcement, not a distinct refusal message; see account-identifier-v1 -> theInteractionWithTheCollapse.

Constraints are credential-store.ts::isSubmittableIdentifier's, restated rather than invented: printable ASCII only, no whitespace, nothing above U+007E, at least one '@'. Normalised NFKC then ASCII-only case folding before hashing — NOT toLowerCase(), which differs between JavaScript and Swift for real characters. IT IS NOT AN ENUMERATION KEY: it selects at most one principal within one named Organization, and a caller who does not already hold it learns nothing from this route.

resolveMemberOutput.description: AT MOST ONE PRINCIPAL, NEVER A SET, AND THE SHAPE ENFORCES IT — this is an object rather than an array precisely so that a future change returning several would be a visible breaking change rather than a quiet widening of a list that was always a list. THE SUBMITTED IDENTIFIER IS NOT ECHOED: the caller sent it and knows it, and echoing it would put an email address in a response body for no purpose and in a log line for anyone who logs responses.

principal_id.description: The value credential-reset-v1 requires and that CR-3 recorded no route produced. This route exists to close that gap without opening enumeration.

role.description: The membership role, returned because an operator about to reset a credential should know whether they are taking over an `owner` or a `member`. That is a fact about the RELATIONSHIP, not about the person, and it changes how carefully the operator should proceed.
